ORCHESTRATION DEFECT CAUGHT AND CORRECTED - 4-digit prefix collision. My board-status script keyed tickets by ticket_id[:4] into a dict, so where two tickets share a 4-hex quad the LAST one silently overwrote the first. Two collisions exist among this epic's children: 4144-2784-6437-4efb (tireless-ruinable-prairiedog, 'Route correctness and edge-cases explicitly and replay block', child of 2ddd) collided with 4144-75d3-6af1-47d3 (tireless-convenable-canvasback, 'enrich gate marker is all-or-nothing', NO parent, not in this epic); and 7931-faee-53ba-47b1 (exciting-arduous-borzoi, this epic's child) collided with 7931-e644-30de-4023 (exciting-chargeable-monarch, child of 86ac).

Impact: the 4144 leaf agent was dispatched with the CORRECT canonical id but the WRONG title/framing taken from the colliding non-child ticket. Corrected by message: told it to discard any conclusions reached against the 'enrich gate marker' framing, re-read 4144-2784-6437-4efb fresh, verify that prefix-keyed prior artifacts (remediation/4144.md) actually belong to it, and noted that the epic names tireless-ruinable-prairiedog as one of the NINE HARDENING children - so the no-behaviour-change and net-negative-lines guarantees do not apply to it. 7931 was unaffected because I worked it inline from its full id.

This is precisely the failure mode AGENTS.md documents when it deprecates the bare 4-digit fragment as a reference form: in a store of this size those quads collide. Lesson for the rest of this run: key by FULL canonical id, and treat any 4-hex-keyed scratch artifact as ambiguous until checked against the ticket.
